newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Notionnel to reach up towards 129.00.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Notionnel to reach up towards 129.00.

text.p: June notionnel futures traded on MATIF will climb towards 129.00 on Wednesday, having broken above a downward channel, technical analysts said on Wednesday.

"We made a pullback to 128.20 and we finished the movement in a small downward channel," said Christian Bado, senior technical analyst at Ferrier Lullin in Geneva. "We have now broken out of that channel and there are further gains to come."
The contract moved down to form a low at 128.20 on Tuesday.
At 0853 GMT, June notionnel futures were at 128.66, up 24 basis points having formed a two basis point gap from Tuesday's close to open at 128.56.
Bado said the lower level of the mark/Paris rate would also help notionnel to move higher.
"We are looking for a move towards 128.84, and possibly 129.00 before moving down again towards 128.20," he said.
The contract formed a low at 128.84 on April 17.
Technical analysts at Chase in London said resistance at 128.88/90 was possible very near term.

"However the decline from 129.38 has breached near term up trendline support weakening the technical outlook," they said in a research note. "Failure to overcome the 128.88/90 barrier will keep the pressure on the downside."
To the downside, Bado said support for this session was at 128.50. If that broke, 128.20 would be a further barrier, analysts said.
"A break below 128.20 will test 128.04 and 127.90 initially. A further break below here will target 127.06," Chase technical analysts said.
At the short end, June Pibor futures were at 96.38, up four basis points on the day.
Richard Adcock, manager of technical research at HSBC Futures in London, said consolidation on Tuesday had pushed Pibor back through 96.40 but prices had failed there.

"Sellers quickly gained the upper hand to see setbacks to the close," he said in a research note. "This confirmed the significance of the overhead supply and the difficulty the market is likely to have pushing through."
Adcock said continued sideways action over the short term, although the longer term view was remained negative.
